Both people observe the initial placement together, and the sender observes the entire later transfer through a view that cannot reveal reader attendance.
The reader retains the last observed location unless they see the transfer or receive a trusted current-location report.
An absent reader sees none of the transfer, receives no update, and does not learn that a transfer occurred.
The sender accepts the particular attendance record as accurate and has no other reader-attendance information; the actual private attendance is hidden.
The attendance record explicitly says the reader watched the entire transfer or did not watch any of it, and records no later update.
Actual attendance and the attendance record vary independently in authoring; the record's possible error is not disclosed to the sender.
Initial and final locations differ in each authored case. This is an authoring invariant, not a rule known to the reader.
Labels mean the fixed place_b proposition under world, reader-belief, or sender-attributed-reader-belief perspective, not belief accuracy.
The base messages contain the scene and a candidate proposition but no perspective question, generated answer, gold bit, planned message, or unknown-future target.
All cases have split fresh and phase prior; the before/after comparison refers to adding a question, not to any change in the characters' evidence.
Authoring rules and review metadata are not model-visible scene instructions.
